added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(I=(M,a,X,Y,c,L,B)\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{exp}}\), let \(C_X\) and \(C_Y\) be the weak components of \(X\) and \(Y\) in the underlying undirected full graph.  Suppose either \(C_X\ne C_Y\), or \(C_X=C_Y=C\) and \(C\) has cycle rank at most one; no restriction is imposed on the other weak components.  Then \(\operatorname{UnicycleHandle}\) is a sound-and-complete polynomial-size certificate calculus and an exact polynomial-time algorithm, with the following explicit branches.

If \(C_X\ne C_Y\), then \(X=a_X\) is not a Beckers actual cause of \(Y=a_Y\), \(C^\star(I)=+\infty\), and the weak-component partition is a separating cut.  If \(C_X=C_Y=C\), the exact global minimum equals the minimum for \(I|_C\), and all other components may be retained at actuality.  When \(C\) has cycle rank zero and \(X\not\leadsto_{G[C]}Y\), the answer is again negative,
\[
 C^\star(I)=+\infty,
\]
and the set of vertices directed-reachable from \(X\) is a separating cut.  Only when \(X\leadsto_{G[C]}Y\) does the unique directed path \(P_0=X\to\cdots\to P_m=Y\) enter the functional, in which case
\[
 C^\star(I)
 =\min_{\substack{s_i\in R(P_i)\setminus\{a_{P_i}\}\\0\le i\le m}}
   \sum_{i=1}^{m} C_i(s_{i-1},s_i).
\]
The value-path compiler and verifier use \(O(L)\) arithmetic and indexed-address operations.  When \(C\) has cycle rank one,
\[
 C^\star(I)=\operatorname{MS}_1(I|_C),
\]
and the exceptional-edge min-sum algorithm uses \(O(L^7)\) arithmetic and indexed-address operations.  In every branch, \(X=a_X\) is a Beckers actual cause of \(Y=a_Y\) if and only if \(C^\star(I)<+\infty\); every finite rational has \(O(B+\log(L+1))\) bits, and the algorithm returns a positive witness with an exact optimum certificate or a polynomial-size separating cut.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The quantity \(C^\star(I)\) is defined independently of the algorithm as the minimum deletion cost among canonical Beckers witnesses, with the empty minimum equal to \(+\infty\).  Because the signature and edge set are finite and every edge cost is a finite nonnegative rational, a witness exists if and only if this minimum is finite.  Consequently
\[
 \mathbf 1\{X=a_X\text{ is a Beckers actual cause of }Y=a_Y\}
 =\mathbf 1\{C^\star(I)<+\infty\}.                                      \tag{1}
\]
This relates the causal query to the optimization functional; it does not define the causal query by the functional.

Let \(C_X\) and \(C_Y\) be as in the statement.  If \(C_X\ne C_Y\), \(\texttt{lem:component-restriction-normalization}\) says directly that no Beckers witness exists.  Equation (1) therefore gives
\[
 C^\star(I)=+\infty.                                                       \tag{2}
\]
By the definition of a weak component, no edge of the underlying undirected graph joins \(C_X\) to its complement.  Hence the partition \((C_X,(U\cup V)\setminus C_X)\), with \(X\in C_X\) and \(Y\notin C_X\), is an explicitly checkable separating cut.  This proves the first branch.

Now suppose \(C_X=C_Y=C\), and write \(I_C=I|_C\).  No vertex of \(C\) has a parent outside \(C\), since such an edge would join the two vertices in the same weak component.  Thus restricting the domains and tables to \(C\) preserves acyclicity, exogenous-root status, totality of every local table, the actual-solution equations, distinctness of \(X,Y\), nonnegative rational costs, and explicit encoding.  Therefore \(I_C\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{exp}}\), with input sizes \(L_C\le L\) and \(B_C\le B\).  The component-normalization lemma gives both existence equivalence and the exact equality
\[
 C^\star(I)=C^\star(I_C).                                                  \tag{3}
\]
It also gives the promised extension: retain every edge outside \(C\) and assign every vertex outside \(C\) its actual value.  Nonnegativity of the costs is already one of that lemma's hypotheses, so (3) includes the cost claim rather than merely the decision claim.

Assume first that \(C\) has cycle rank zero.  Its underlying undirected graph is connected by the definition of \(C\), and a connected graph of cycle rank zero is a tree: if an undirected cycle existed, deleting one edge of that cycle would preserve connectedness and contradict \(|E|=|C|-1\); conversely a connected acyclic graph has \(|E|=|C|-1\) by induction after removing a leaf.  Hence the full graph of \(I_C\) is a polyforest, so \(I_C\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{forest}}\).

Suppose \(X\not\leadsto_{G[C]}Y\).  Applying \(\texttt{thm:value-path-optimum}\) to \(I_C\) proves that no Beckers witness exists on \(C\).  Let
\[
 S=\{q\in C:X\leadsto_{G[C]}q\}\cup\{X\}.                               \tag{4}
\]
Then \(X\in S\), \(Y\notin S\), and there is no directed edge \(p\to q\) with \(p\in S\) and \(q\in C\setminus S\): such an edge would append to a directed path witnessing \(p\in S\) and would put \(q\) in \(S\).  Thus (4) is the claimed directed-reachability separating cut.  Combining the negative conclusion with (1) and (3) proves
\[
 C^\star(I)=C^\star(I_C)=+\infty.                                         \tag{5}
\]
This is the subcase that must be decided before any value-path object is formed.

Suppose instead that \(X\leadsto_{G[C]}Y\).  Since the underlying graph is a tree, there is only one undirected \(X\)-to-\(Y\) path; the directed path is therefore unique and may be written \(P_0=X\to\cdots\to P_m=Y\).  The exact-optimum part of \(\texttt{thm:value-path-optimum}\), followed by (3), gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 C^\star(I)
 &=C^\star(I_C)\\
 &=\min_{\substack{s_i\in R(P_i)\setminus\{a_{P_i}\}\\0\le i\le m}}
   \sum_{i=1}^{m}C_i(s_{i-1},s_i).                         \tag{6}
 \end{aligned}
\]
The same theorem proves that finiteness of (6) is equivalent to a value-path certificate and hence, by (1), to the causal query.  Applying \(\texttt{thm:compiler-verifier-equivalence}\) to \(I_C\) yields the positive, exact-optimum, or layerwise separating certificate, uses \(O(L_C)\subseteq O(L)\) arithmetic and indexed-address operations, and gives the stated bit bound.  A positive certificate is extended globally by the construction following (3).  A negative certificate remains globally separating because the component lemma rules out every global witness whenever it rules out a witness on \(C\).

Finally suppose that \(C\) has cycle rank one.  The restricted instance \(I_C\) meets every premise of \(\texttt{lem:connected-unicycle-min-sum}\).  The normalized tuples in that lemma are exactly the feasible tuples in \(\mathrm{def:rank\mbox{-}one\mbox{-}min\mbox{-}sum\mbox{-}functional}\): if their row-difference set is legal, the repair variable is \(\bot\); if it is illegal, the unique exceptional edge is deleted while its complementary directed arc is intact, and the repair variable chooses one edge on that arc.  The retained-parent hitting constraints are identical to those in the definition, and the support-row constraints are identical as well.  Therefore the normalization direction of the lemma gives
\[
 \operatorname{MS}_1(I_C)\le C^\star(I_C),                                 \tag{7}
\]
whereas its converse maps every feasible tuple defining \(\operatorname{MS}_1(I_C)\) to a Beckers witness of exactly the displayed deletion cost and gives
\[
 C^\star(I_C)\le\operatorname{MS}_1(I_C).                                  \tag{8}
\]
Equations (3), (7), and (8) prove the explicit identifying equality
\[
 C^\star(I)=\operatorname{MS}_1(I_C).                                       \tag{9}
\]
The same lemma partitions the legality alternatives into at most \(2|E(K)|-1\) min-sum programs, evaluates them in \(O(L_C^7)\subseteq O(L^7)\) arithmetic and indexed-address operations, bounds every finite rational by \(O(B_C+\log(L_C+1))\subseteq O(B+\log(L+1))\) bits, and returns either a witness with exact optimum data or infeasibility tables forming a separating cut.  Extension or separation for the global instance again follows from (3).

Computing weak components, cycle rank, and the reachable set (4) requires one scan of the explicitly indexed vertices and edges, hence \(O(L)\) address operations.  The forest branch is therefore linear-arithmetic, and the rank-one branch dominates the uniform bound by \(O(L^7)\).  All recorded assignments, support rows, predecessor choices, message tables, and cuts occur in the explicit finite tables considered by the cited compiler or min-sum lemma, so their lengths are polynomial in \(L+B\).  This proves soundness, completeness, exact optimality, and all certificate and complexity claims.

Two smallest exact checks isolate the repaired split.  In the deterministic binary tree \(Z\to X\), \(Z\to Y\), with actual world zero and equations \(X=Z\), \(Y=Z\), intervention \(X\leftarrow1\) leaves \(Y=0\).  Here the set (4) is \(\{X\}\), so (5) correctly returns \(+\infty\).  In the deterministic binary chain \(X\to Y\), with actual world zero and equation \(Y=X\), intervention \(X\leftarrow1\) gives \(Y=1\); the unique transition has \(C_1(1,1)=0\), so (6) returns zero.  Thus the no-directed-path and directed-path branches differ already on the smallest connected forests and cannot be merged.
added_lemmas.justification: The theorem identifies the exact relevant-component frontier and exposes the directed-reachability failure branch before the path functional is formed.
added_lemmas.gap: Existing Halpern--Pearl causal-tree algorithms do not establish component restriction, full-graph reachability legality, actualized projection, or the rank-one exceptional-edge program for Beckers causation.
added_lemmas.consumer: The result gives the explicit-support backend a complete dispatcher returning a witness and exact optimum certificate or a separating cut whenever the relevant full-graph component has cycle rank at most one.

proposed_core_edits.name: Cstar

proposed.name: Cstar
proposed.def: For \(I=(M,a,X,Y,c,L,B)\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{exp}}\), \(C^\star(I)\) is the minimum of \(\sum_{e\in E(G)\setminus E(H)}c(e)\) over canonical Beckers witnesses with retained graph \(H\in\mathcal H(G)\); the empty minimum is \(+\infty\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The strengthened frontier needs a causal minimum-cost target defined on the whole explicit class, including negative and rank-one branches where the forest-only symbol \(\operatorname{OPT}\) is not defined.

proposed_core_edits.name: MSone

proposed.name: MSone
proposed.def: \(\operatorname{MS}_1(J)\) is the finite normalized-tuple optimization defined by \(\mathrm{def:rank\mbox{-}one\mbox{-}min\mbox{-}sum\mbox{-}functional}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The rank-one branch needs a named, explicit optimization functional distinct from the causal optimum whose equality to it is proved by normalization and converse reconstruction.

proposed.name: Connected rank-one normalized min-sum functional
proposed.construction:
For a restricted instance \(J=I|_C\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{exp}}\) whose underlying undirected full graph is connected and has cycle rank one, let \(K\) be its unique simple cycle.  If there is an edge \(e^\star\in E(K)\) for which \(K\setminus\{e^\star\}\) is a directed path from the tail of \(e^\star\) to its head, use that edge; if no such edge exists, write \(e^\star=\bot\).  Put \(U_C=U\cap C\) and \(V_C=V\cap C\).  For \(w\in R(C)\) and rows \(\rho_Z\in R(\operatorname{Pa}_{G[C]}(Z))\), \(Z\in V_C\setminus\{X\}\), define
\[
 D^0(w,\rho)=\{p\to Z\in E(G[C]):Z\ne X,\ \rho_{Z,p}\ne w_p\}.
\]
The repair choice is \(f=\bot\) whenever \(e^\star=\bot\) or \(D^0(w,\rho)\) satisfies
\[
 e^\star\notin D^0(w,\rho)
 \quad\text{or}\quad
 D^0(w,\rho)\cap\bigl(E(K)\setminus\{e^\star\}\bigr)\ne\varnothing;
\]
otherwise \(f\) ranges over \(E(K)\setminus\{e^\star\}\).  Let \(D_f=D^0(w,\rho)\) for \(f=\bot\), and let \(D_f=D^0(w,\rho)\cup\{f\}\) otherwise.  For \(Z\in V_C\), put
\[
 S_Z(D_f)=\{p\in\operatorname{Pa}_{G[C]}(Z):p\to Z\notin D_f\}.
\]
Then \(\operatorname{MS}_1(J)\) is the minimum of \(\sum_{e\in D_f}c(e)\) over \((w,\rho,f)\) satisfying
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 w_{U_C}=a_{U_C},\qquad w_X\ne a_X,\qquad w_Y\ne a_Y,\\
 w_Z\in A_Z(\rho_Z)\quad(Z\in V_C\setminus\{X\}),\\
 S_Z(D_f)\cap\Delta\ne\varnothing
 \quad\bigl(Z\in V_C,\ \Delta\in\mathcal B_Z\bigr).
 \end{gathered}
\]
The empty minimum is \(+\infty\).  Thus the variables, objective, support constraints, actual-row hitting constraints, and exceptional-edge legality repair are all part of the definition.

proposed_core_edits.reason: This exposes all optimization variables, support and hitting constraints, legality repair, objective, and empty-minimum convention used by the relevant-component theorem.

proposed_core_edits.name: UnicycleHandle

proposed.name: UnicycleHandle
proposed.def: Identify the weak full-graph components of \(X\) and \(Y\); return a component cut if they differ; on a common rank-zero component, return a directed-reachability cut unless \(X\) reaches \(Y\), and only then run the value-path compiler; on a common rank-one component run the exceptional-edge min-sum program; retain every other component at actuality.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The prior handle sent every rank-zero common component directly to the value-path compiler and omitted the required no-directed-path branch.

proposed.name: Relevant-component forest/unicycle handle
proposed.construction: Given an explicit instance, compute the weak components of the underlying undirected full graph and let \(C_X\) and \(C_Y\) contain \(X\) and \(Y\).  If \(C_X\ne C_Y\), \(\operatorname{UnicycleHandle}\) returns the weak-component separating cut.  If \(C_X=C_Y=C\) and \(C\) has cycle rank zero, it first computes directed reachability from \(X\) in \(G[C]\): when \(Y\) is unreachable it returns that directed-reachability cut and value \(+\infty\), and only when \(Y\) is reachable does it invoke the value-path compiler on the unique directed path.  If the common component has cycle rank one, it cuts the unique factor-graph cycle at a boundary variable and carries the exceptional-edge mode---shortcut retained, complementary arc already broken, or one specified repair edge---jointly with the local nonactual-value state.  Every other weak component is retained at its actual assignment.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The construction must explicitly test directed reachability in the rank-zero common-component branch before invoking a path-indexed functional.
The proved replacement strictly subsumes the global-unicycle theorem, handles arbitrary irrelevant components, and includes the missing rank-zero directed-reachability subcase.
The forest-only symbol \(\operatorname{OPT}\) does not denote the negative or rank-one branches of the strengthened relevant-component result.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: On the relevant-component cycle-rank-at-most-one class, let \(C_X,C_Y\) be the weak components of \(X,Y\).  Then \(C^\star(I)=+\infty\) if \(C_X\ne C_Y\), and, for \(C_X=C_Y=C\), \(C^\star(I)=+\infty\) when \(C\) has cycle rank zero and \(X\not\leadsto_{G[C]}Y\); \(C^\star(I)=\min_{s_i\in R(P_i)\setminus\{a_{P_i}\}}\sum_{i=1}^m C_i(s_{i-1},s_i)\) when \(C\) has cycle rank zero and \(X\leadsto_{G[C]}Y\); and \(C^\star(I)=\operatorname{MS}_1(I|_C)\) when \(C\) has cycle rank one.  In every branch, existence is equivalent to \(C^\star(I)<+\infty\).
proposed_core_edits.reason: The headline functional must split disconnected components and rank-zero directed nonreachability from the path calculation, while retaining the explicit rank-one optimization.

prose_updates.tldr: Beckers defines actual causation by counterfactual dependence in an actualized structural simplification, but the definition itself gives no exact algorithmic frontier. Under finite explicit local tables, the project proves a relevant-component frontier: the answer is immediately negative when \(X\) and \(Y\) lie in different weak full-graph components; otherwise arbitrary unrelated components are harmless, and an exact certificate calculus is polynomial whenever their common component has cycle rank at most one. A rank-zero component first yields a directed-reachability cut when \(X\) cannot reach \(Y\), and only a reachable instance invokes the linear-arithmetic value-path compiler; a rank-one component uses the exceptional-edge min-sum program. The backend returns a witness and exact optimum certificate or a separating cut. A shared-selector construction separately proves NP-completeness even for deterministic binary models whose endogenous graph is one directed chain, showing why the positive full-graph restriction is substantive.

project_justification.niche: The novel computational scope uses finite explicitly encoded tables and restricts only the weak full-graph component relevant to \(X\) and \(Y\): disconnected queries are rejected by a component cut, while a common component of cycle rank zero or one is tractable even if every other component is unrestricted. This is a full-graph condition on \(U\cup V\), not the published endogenous causal-tree condition for Halpern--Pearl causation.
project_justification.fill: The project proves component restriction with cost preservation, an explicit three-way frontier functional, a linear-arithmetic value-path compiler after a directed-reachability test, and an exact exceptional-edge min-sum algorithm for a connected rank-one component. Independently checkable positive, optimality, and negative certificates accompany the result. The restricted chain reduction and shared-selector obstruction establish the complementary Beckers hardness phenomenon without claiming unrestricted counting or general treewidth tractability.

prose_updates.related_work: Beckers2025Actual, Section 5.1, Definitions 13, 15, and 16 on pages 523--524 and Section 6, Definitions 18 and 19 and Proposition 20 on page 525, supplies the structural-simplification and actual-causation semantics implemented here; the proof of Proposition 20 appears on page 532. It contains neither a compiler nor the relevant-component complexity frontier. Beckers2025NCM supplies set-valued equations and topological counterfactual semantics, while finite explicit encoding is this project's computational-scope restriction. The earlier UAI version of EiterLukasiewicz2006Tractable, Section 4.1 and Theorems 4.2--4.3, is the closest methodological comparator: its Halpern--Pearl causal-tree analysis propagates subsets of endogenous path-variable domains. The present positive theorem instead audits Beckers actualized projection and deletion legality on the full graph, first separating directed nonreachability in a forest component and then extending exact computation through one full-graph cycle by an exceptional-edge state. The shared-selector proposition shows only that transferring the unaugmented endogenous-only state type loses full-exogenous reachability information; it does not modify the published Halpern--Pearl theorem. EiterLukasiewicz2002Complexity and AleksandrowiczEtAl2014 show that complexity depends on the causation definition, but neither treats Beckers deletion. IbrahimRehwaldPretschner2019SAT and IbrahimPretschner2020Optimization address Boolean Halpern--Pearl encodings and objectives, and ReydDiaconescuDessalles2025Search gives approximate Halpern--Pearl-style search; none supplies the arbitrary-domain exact Beckers certificates proved here.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The positive theorem requires finite explicitly indexed local tables and that the common weak full-graph component of \(X\) and \(Y\) have cycle rank at most one; it makes no claim for relevant components of larger cycle rank, general full-graph treewidth, succinct mechanisms, continuous domains, or negative deletion costs. The hardness theorem concerns a broader Beckers class described by an endogenous chain and shared exogenous selectors, not the positive relevant-component class. The selector reduction gives a bijection only for normalized certificates; unrestricted successful retained graphs need not be counted parsimoniously.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The exact tractability statement is component-local: different weak components give a negative answer, and when \(X\) and \(Y\) share a component, all other components may be retained at their actual assignments regardless of their cycle structure. A common rank-zero component is split again by full directed reachability; no path means value \(+\infty\), whereas a path activates the unique-path functional. A common rank-one component is handled by the proved normalized min-sum functional and exceptional-edge legality modes. These are restrictions on the full graph over \(U\cup V\), not assumptions inherited from Beckers or the endogenous causal-tree class of Eiter--Lukasiewicz. The explicit-table, finite-domain, acyclic, total-table, actual-solution, and nonnegative-rational-cost conditions remain in force. No general treewidth fixed-parameter algorithm or unrestricted parsimonious certificate-counting theorem is claimed.
